steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station H-01, survey area H. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 332.5 | 0.52 | 0.52
2 | 601.3 | 6.89 | 7.41
3 | 359.9 | 16.01 | 23.42
4 | 286.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as K-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station H-01, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station H-01, Survey Area H**

The interpreted resistivity model comprises four layers: a thin surface layer (332.5 Ω·m, 0.52 m), underlain by a more resistive second layer (601.3 Ω·m, 6.89 m), followed by a moderately resistive third layer (359.9 Ω·m, 16.01 m), and a lower-resistivity basal layer (286.0 Ω·m, semi-infinite).

Applying standard VES curve-type notation: layers 1-2-3 (332.5 < 601.3 > 359.9) give a K segment, and layers 2-3-4 (601.3 > 359.9 > 286.0) give a Q segment. The resulting curve type is therefore **KQ**, not a pure K-type as stated in the file. The on-file classification does not account for the resistivity decrease through layers 2–3–4, which defines a Q segment. Recommend updating the interpretation record to reflect the correct KQ curve type for accurate hydrogeological correlation.

{"curve_type_stated": "KQ", "label_issue_flagged": true}
